courses.subject: CHED
courses.title: Guided Study in Issues of Child Development
courses.description:
This course is an application of a student-orientated approach to teaching intended to nurture students to become independent learners, professional teachers of young children, and reflective early childhood education practitioners. Students are required to pursue an issue of child development of their choice, build their understanding of the issue, and then share their personal views of the issue.

Students’ performance is assessed according to their demonstration of logical thinking and thorough analysis of various issues from different theoretical perspectives with the support of empirical evidence.
courses.course_syllabus:
Students take the initiation to select issue topics to be explored in this course. Examples of categories of issues are as follows:

A. Effective Caring, e.g.,

- Responsive caring and quality of adult-child relationship

- Constructive guidance and discipline

B. Effective Learning, e.g.,

- Playing and exploring

- Learner-centered pedagogical practices

- Use of technology and media

- Moral and character education

C. Knowing Atypical Child Development, e.g.,

- Disabilities/disorder

- Child abuse

D. Professional Development, e.g.,

- Teachers’ knowledge and beliefs

- Early childhood teachers’ development and preparation
courses.feedback_evaluation: Feedback from students will be collected through email exchanges and course-end evaluation.
courses.required_readings: To be assigned according to the selected topics
